answer: Each registered identity must lock a bond of 500 tokens and present a one-per-hardware credential derived from a device secret, so one machine yields one registry entry. Creating a fake identity locks 500 tokens for 30 epochs, and a proven sybil claim slashes 80 percent of the bond. Splitting or copying identities raises marginal cost per fake entry, and detection by independent jurors drawn from a tundra, nebula, or fable pool shares the penalty across the attacker's whole cluster.
